PullRequest.Title: sessions: add row actions to artifact details lists
PullRequest.Body:

## What

Rows in the artifact details lists (the context view above the Agents window chat input) can now have actions. They show in a floating action bar at the right of the row, inside the row. The GitHub pull request integration uses this for:

- **Rerun Check** on failed checks of an open PR's current commit, when the check is a GitHub Actions job in the PR's own repository. It reruns that one job, and declines with a reason while the rest of the workflow is still running.
- **Resolve Comment** on unresolved review threads. A resolved thread disappears as soon as GitHub confirms the resolve, rather than at the next poll.

## How it works

- **Contract** (`artifactIntegration.ts`):
  - `ArtifactDetails` can declare `itemActions` (id, label, icon), and each item lists the action IDs that currently apply to it.
  - `IArtifactDetailsModel` gains an optional `runItemAction(itemId, actionId, token)`. The integration rechecks that the action still applies to the item and rejects with a readable reason otherwise.
- **Transport:** item actions run directly through the details lease, like Load More. The only additions are one `runItemAction` protocol request and forwarding in the service's details wrappers.
- **No executor:** item actions skip the run executor on purpose, so they never wait for or block artifact actions. For example, you can resolve a comment while an Address Comments turn is running. The trade-off is that they have no Activities history, automation or uncertain-outcome tracking. The contract comment and the design doc limit them to effects that are safe to repeat.
- **Hiding resolved threads (PR integration):**
  - A thread you resolved stays hidden until GitHub reports it resolved or removed, so a lagging read can't bring it back.
  - The comment count, the comments list, Address Comments, automation and the repair prompt all read threads through one helper, so they stay consistent.
  - If GitHub still reports the thread unresolved in a read 30 seconds or more later, it is treated as reopened and shown again.
- **UI** (`artifactDetailsList.ts`, `artifactStateLists.ts`, `artifactDetailsModel.ts`):
  - The action bar shows on hover, focus or selection. Item hovers are attached to the row's text so they don't compete with the action buttons' hovers.
  - Progress is per item, and keyboard focus is kept when rows update or are removed. Clicking an action doesn't open the item or close the panel.
  - Screen readers hear when an action completes, failures show the usual error notification, and the accessibility help and accessible view describe the new actions.

Not included: extension-provided integrations can't offer item actions yet (that needs a proposed-API change), and agent tools don't list or run them.

## How to test

With `chat.artifactIntegrations.enabled` on, record a GitHub PR with failing Actions checks and unresolved review comments as an artifact in the Agents window, then open its details:

1. On the Checks tab, hover or focus a failed check, then click **Rerun Check**.
2. On the Comments tab, click **Resolve Comment**. The row should disappear immediately and focus should move to the next comment.
3. Use the keyboard: Tab from a list reaches the focused row's actions, and Enter runs one.

## Validation

Run with Node 24.22.0, as `.nvmrc` requires.

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>`: passed, no warnings.
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot` on the related suites listed below: **448 passing**.
  - `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/{artifactIntegrationServerTools,clientArtifactIntegrationEndpoint,githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration}.test.ts`
  - `src/vs/platform/artifactIntegrations/test/browser/localArtifactIntegrationHost.test.ts`
  - `src/vs/platform/artifactIntegrations/test/common/{artifactIntegrationProtocol,artifactIntegrations,compositeArtifactModel}.test.ts`
  - `src/vs/platform/artifactIntegrations/test/node/artifactIntegrationStorage.test.ts`
  - `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/{artifactIntegrationPresentation,sessionArtifacts,sessionChatInputToolbar}.test.ts`
  - `src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostArtifactIntegrations.test.ts`
  - `src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadChatArtifactIntegrations.test.ts`
  - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatArtifactActionContentPart.test.ts`
- The new test for immediately hiding resolved threads was confirmed to fail without the fix.

New tests cover:
- the protocol round-trip and validation of item-action references;
- what the PR integration offers, its skip reasons and GitHub calls, that no run records are created, and that it runs while an artifact action is busy;
- immediate thread hiding, including lagging and reopened reads;
- with real CSS: row action layout, per-item progress, focus retention and moving focus after a row is removed, and failure reporting.

Not run:
- Component explorer screenshots of the two new fixtures (`PullRequestCheckRowActions`, `PullRequestCommentRowActions`). Their dev-server dependencies could not be installed locally because of a registry authentication error (`E401`). The Screenshots CI check will capture them.
- Integration and smoke suites, and live GitHub calls.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added call, resource interests, and refresh implementation establish the exact synchronous call path and fragment set. The only magnitude uncertainty is GitHub/network latency and how many pages a particular PR's review threads require; the unrelated calls and critical-path wait occur on every rerun click.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub GraphQL/REST requests and response bytes for pull-request core, review threads, checks, mergeability, job, run, and rerun operations.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every rerun click adds four pull-request fragment fetches before three Actions API requests; review-thread work grows by pages of 100 threads and additional comment pages, and repeated/concurrent clicks repeat or restart authoritative reads.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased action latency and excessive network I/O on the critical path.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no per-check row action placing a whole authoritative PR refresh on this interaction path; existing details observation relied on the polling subscription rather than a user click forcing all fragments.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each new Rerun Check row action now performs an authoritative whole-pull-request refresh, then performs getJob, getRun, and rerunJob. The whole refresh includes review-thread and mergeability reads that are not used by rerun validation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line `const snapshot = await this.resource.refresh(token);` in `rerunCheck` invokes the resource-wide refresh before any job validation. `GitHubPullRequestArtifactResource.refresh` calls `subscription.refresh(undefined, ..., { authoritative: true })`; the subscription's effective interests are core, reviewThreads (with bodies), checks (including optional), and mergeability, and `refreshSubscription` fetches core then awaits all other effective fragments.
Findings.Title: Limit rerun revalidation to core and checks
Findings.Impact: Clicking Rerun Check is delayed by unrelated GitHub reads and consumes extra API/rate-limit capacity; on PRs with large review histories, pagination can make a simple job rerun noticeably slow. Rapid reruns on different rows can further cancel/restart authoritative fragment reads.
Findings.Evidence: `rerunCheck` awaits `resource.refresh` before deriving `headSha` and the check. The unchanged refresh implementation passes no fragment, so `PullRequestResourceService.refreshSubscription` fetches core and then `Promise.all`s every effective fragment. This binding subscribes to reviewThreads with bodies, all checks, and mergeability. Review threads are fetched 100 per GraphQL page (and comments can paginate), so a large review history adds multiple unrelated network requests and the action waits for their completion before its three Actions API calls.
Findings.Recommendation: Refresh only the authoritative data required for this mutation—core followed by checks—then keep the existing getJob/getRun/rerunJob validation. Expose a fragment-scoped resource refresh (or equivalent sequential core/check refresh) so reviewThreads and mergeability remain off this critical path; coalesce concurrent core/check refreshes if multiple rows are invoked.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and interact with pull-request details lists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the details panel acquires details leases and projects current observable data before rendering. Subsequent polling updates reproject the list; hidden action bars are constructed only for rendered rows. No new filesystem, subprocess, database, or direct network operation was added to the synchronous browser render path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire and observe artifact details through the integration service/protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing details-subscription acquisition per displayed details section; provider updates cross the existing integration transport. No per-row IPC is performed during rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same details sections and updates already crossed this boundary; the diff enriches their payload with item-action metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Lease acquisition is required to populate the panel; row action projection/rendering remains local after each update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 200 items in a details page, with effective DOM/action-bar work limited to currently rendered rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One details lease per referenced section is retained by the model. Focus/action update events fan out only to rendered row templates; the virtual list bounds active DOM rows.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The details lease observes the existing pull-request resource cache/polling subscription. Item descriptors and buttons are rebuilt from the current observable details; no new persistent cache is introduced. Lists are capped at 200 items per page and rendered by a virtualized WorkbenchList.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that action projection is O(items × listed actions) and row updates are limited by list virtualization; with the 200-item validation cap and current one-action descriptors, this is bounded local work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact visible-row count and update frequency depend on panel size and PR polling state, but both are bounded and did not establish a reportable UI regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: added allocation and action-bar work is bounded by validated page size and virtualized visible rows, with no new expensive boundary per row.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rerun a failed GitHub Actions check
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click crosses the item-action protocol, then synchronously awaits a whole PR refresh (core, reviewThreads, checks, mergeability), getJob, getRun, and rerunJob. Every refresh fragment must settle before job validation begins, including unrelated fragments.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch item ID and action ID through the details subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to dispatch the action to the agent host; small relative to network work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authoritatively refresh the entire subscribed pull-request snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four fragment fetches per click: core first, then reviewThreads, checks, and mergeability; reviewThreads/checks paginate in pages of 100 and review-thread comments can require additional pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-check row interaction forced a whole authoritative pull-request refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All are awaited before job-specific validation; reviewThreads and mergeability are unrelated to rerunning a check.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Confirm job identity and workflow completion, then request a job rerun.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three Actions API operations per successful click: getJob, getRun, rerunJob.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The row action and these job-specific calls did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequential validation/mutation required after current core/check data is established.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rerun clicks and, for unrelated review-thread work, pages of 100 threads/comments; different failed-check rows can be invoked concurrently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Different rows can run concurrently because busy state is per item. The pull-request service serializes each fragment by cancellation/restart rather than coalescing authoritative callers; Actions API calls proceed per surviving action without a shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The action intentionally requests an authoritative refresh, so warm fragment state and normal polling freshness do not avoid network reads. Job/run validation has no cache. Concurrent authoritative refreshes are not coalesced; an authoritative request cancels an existing fragment operation and starts another.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added call passes no fragment, the resource subscribes to four fragments, and refreshSubscription explicitly awaits core then every effective fragment.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub latency, rate-limit state, and review-history page count vary, but the whole-refresh fan-out and wait are unconditional on every click.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium boundary fan-out: unrelated review-thread and mergeability fetches are newly placed on the rerun critical path and can paginate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve a review comment from its row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click crosses one item-action protocol request and awaits one resolveThread mutation. UI removal follows the response; the invalidated review-thread read is scheduled afterward and is off the mutation's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch Resolve Comment through the details lease.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatches the mutation and is required for progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the GraphQL review thread and invalidate its observed fragment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GitHub review-thread mutation per user click, followed by one scheduled reviewThreads invalidation/read shared through the pull-request resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No row-level mutation occurred; thread reads came from normal polling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The mutation is critical; the refreshed thread list is off the immediate UI-removal path because the local map hides the row.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of user-invoked thread resolutions before GitHub observations catch up; retained state is bounded by threads in the active PR/binding lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Busy state is per thread, so manually invoked different threads may run concurrently; there is no loop or automatic fan-out. Each successful resolution adds one bounded map entry until a subsequent complete observation prunes it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Availability is checked against the current observed thread snapshot. After a successful mutation, a local resolved-thread map hides the row until a complete GitHub read confirms resolution/removal or a later unresolved observation indicates reopening. Invalidation schedules only the reviewThreads fragment.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the mutation cardinality is one per click and that invalidation is fragment-scoped; no automatic collection fan-out is present.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A user can manually resolve several rows quickly, but realistic concurrency requires one click per thread and retained entries are pruned by complete observations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the required mutation is one per explicit click, refresh is fragment-scoped and off the immediate UI-removal path, and temporary retained state has a defined pruning lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mark a draft pull request ready
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The artifact action awaits the same markReadyForReview network mutation as before. API-client acquisition and authentication validation wrap the existing request; invalidation occurs after success and schedules existing fragment refresh behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mark the pull request ready and refresh affected fragments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GitHub mutation per Mark Ready invocation, followed by invalidation of core and mergeability.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior resource callback acquired the same repository API client, issued the same mutation, and invalidated the same fragments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The mutation is critical; invalidation refresh is scheduled after it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation at a time under existing action execution controls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Execution remains under the existing artifact-action executor/sequencing; this diff does not add per-item concurrency to Mark Ready.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The API client is acquired for the current account and disposed after the operation. Pull-request core/mergeability cache invalidation remains after success, matching prior behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the before/after callback bodies and moved invalidation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to PR causality; wrapper placement changed but boundary count did not.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: the refactor preserves remote-call cardinality and cache invalidation behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files. One actionable network boundary-fan-out was reported on Rerun Check; UI projection, protocol forwarding, resolved-thread retention/pruning, and the Mark Ready refactor were bounded or preserved prior boundary behavior.
